title: Purchase-price allocation: the source’s six-step outline
rows: Identify the purchase price, including cash and equity consideration
Review net book value: balance sheet, write-offs, impairments and write-ups
Estimate fair-value adjustments to acquired tangible assets
Identify acquired intangible value: brand, technology, customer relationships and other identifiable items
Estimate intangible fair values using appropriate methods, including the source’s DCF, MPEEM and RRM labels
Compare purchase price with fair-valued net assets and examine goodwill, WARA and deferred tax
note: Recreated from the source diagram. MPEEM means multi-period excess earnings method; RRM means relief-from-royalty method. WARA is weighted average return on assets. These method labels do not supply inputs or make a complete IFRS 3 allocation; see the accounting limitations.

title: Master budget: operating assumptions connect to financial planning
rows: Sales forecast → revenue budget → production budget
Production budget → direct-material budget, direct-labour budget and manufacturing-overhead budget
Resource budgets → cost of goods manufactured / cost of goods sold budget → operating cash budget
Revenue assumptions → selling and administration (SG&A) budget → operating cash budget
CAPEX budget ↔ cash budget ↔ the source box labelled “Financial budget”; these feed budgeted financial statements
note: The right-hand box repeats the “Financial budget” label under the same heading; it may intend a funding/financing budget, but that wording is not silently substituted. The arrows are conceptual dependencies, not completed numerical schedules.

title: A financial-analysis scorecard
rows: Gross profit margin; operating profit margin; net profit margin; return on assets; return on equity
AR turnover; inventory turnover; AP turnover; asset turnover
Current ratio; quick ratio; cash conversion cycle (DSO + DIO − DPO)
Debt to assets; debt to equity; debt-service coverage; fixed-charge coverage; interest coverage
Ratio, sensitivity and scenario analysis, including cash-flow analysis
note: The source groups related questions rather than supplying a weighted score or a financial-health diagnosis. The individual formula definitions and conventions are reviewed separately.

title: Transfer-pricing lifecycle: a repeating review process
note: The source arrows return from audits/dispute resolution to strategy and policies. This is a conceptual workflow; it does not determine a transfer price or replace jurisdiction-specific requirements.

title: Finance organization: functions, relationships and skills
rows: Direct and oversee company financial activities
Manage cash, foreign-exchange risk, financing and investment
Risk management; strategic thinking; banking and financing knowledge
Financial modelling and analysis; negotiation; project management; organization
Technical knowledge; financial software; internal control
Manage financial analysis, budgeting and forecasting
Accounting knowledge; accounting software; regulatory knowledge
Prepare provisions, returns and reports; address tax issues
Work with operating departments; manage and prioritize demand
Gather, analyse, compile and structure data; manage BI software, dashboards and reports
Data analytics; BI software; visualization; demand management
note: All role labels, responsibilities, skills and visible reporting groupings are retained in a readable comparison. This is one source organization example, not a required company hierarchy or current job specification.

title: Value creation: the capitals, business model and feedback context
rows: Financial; manufactured; intellectual; human; social and relationship; natural
Positive or negative effects over short, medium and long terms
The same six capital categories may be affected; no numerical increase is implied
Mission and vision; governance; external environment
Risks and opportunities; strategy and resource allocation; performance; outlook connect around the business model
Value creation, preservation, diminution or erosion
note: The source uses a ring and arrows to connect strategy, performance and outlook with the model. The reconstruction retains the relationships in text; it is not an impact-scoring system.

title: From inputs to outcomes: distinguish organizational and customer value
rows: Inputs (costs): society/organization draws on financial, manufactured, human, intellectual, social and natural capital
Value-adding activities: organization and society consume or transform inputs
Outputs (revenue): products or services; the source marks value added by the organization across the input/activity/output span
Outcomes: effects for the customer, organization and society across all six capitals; the source marks value to the customer between output and outcome
note: This is a qualitative value model. Costs, revenue, customer value and societal outcomes are related concepts, not interchangeable financial quantities.
